newsitem.title: USA: Biopsys responds to FDA on labeling.
newsitem.headline: Biopsys responds to FDA on labeling.

text.p: Biopsys Medical Inc said Tuesday it responded to requests from the United States Food and Drug Administration about the labeling and promotion of its Mammotome Biopsy System.

Biopsys has during the past several months engaged in discussions and correspondence with the FDA's 510(k) Reviewing Division regarding the Mammotome system and the FDA's concerns that devices cleared under 510(k) premarket notifications for diagnostic tissue sampling are being used for excision of tissue.

The FDA has expressed concern that the use of such devices for excision implies a broader, therapeutic application. The discussions between the company and the FDA have been in the context of a review by the FDA of breast biopsy devices. This review included an FDA advisory panel hearing meeting regarding these devices on November 19, 1996.

The company's discussions with the Reviewing Division resulted in defining the procedural steps necessary to fulfill the agency's requests and desire to establish consistent indications and promotional materials for all breast biopsy devices. As a result, on February 3 and 4, Biopsys advised the FDA that it would comply with the requests and file a stand alone 510(k) application for the Mammotome specifically directed towards breast biopsy for diagnostic purposes.

The company committed to file the stand alone 510(k) application within four weeks of February 4, 1997. However, on February 5 the company received a warning letter from a different Division than the one involved in previous discussions. The letter concerned the labeling and promotion of the Company's Mammotome Biopsy System.

"We received the FDA's warning letter from the Office of Compliance on February 5 after filing our commitment to comply with the FDA's 510(k) Reviewing Division's request. We intend to satisfy the Office of Compliance's requirements and fully support the Agency's efforts to create consistent labeling for all breast biopsy devices," stated Steven L. Gex, President and CEO of Biopsys.

"We believe that the commitments already made to the FDA should help to provide a resolution of the principal issues identified in the warning letter. However, the Company cannot predict how long it will take for resolution of these matters. We currently believe that resolution of these matters with the FDA will not have a material impact on our Company's operations," Gex concluded.
